chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdullah via an upraising chain, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, some people will be brought upon stages of light, their faces glittering like the moon on the night of the full moon; the first [generations] and the last [generations] will envy them.' Then he fell silent, then repeated the statement three times. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'My father and mother be sacrificed for you, are they the martyrs?' He said: 'They are the martyrs, but not the martyrs that you think.' He said: 'Are they the prophets?' He said: 'They are the prophets, but not the prophets that you think.' He said: 'Are they the successors?' He said: 'They are the successors, but not the successors that you think.' He said: 'Are they from the people of the sky or the people of the earth?' He said: 'They are from the people of the earth.' He said: 'Then inform me, who are they?' He said: 'And he pointed his hand to Ali (peace be upon him) and said: This one and his Shia. No one from Quraysh hates him except the bastard, nor from the Ansar except the Jew, nor from the Arabs except the whoreson, nor from the rest of the people except the wretched. O Umar! He who claims that he loves me while he hates Ali is lying.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the people envied on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith from Fadail al-Shia?
ai.summary: In Fadail al-Shia, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to establish the theological concept of 'Shi'a' as a distinct, honored community defined by love for Ali (as) rather than mere lineage. The Prophet’s clarification that these figures are 'from the earth' highlights their earthly origin and tangible presence, while the specific exclusions of 'Safahi' (illegitimate), 'Yahudi' (Jewish in spirit), 'Da'i' (imposter), and 'Shaqi' (wretched) provide a nuanced Shia sociological classification of their detractors. This narration serves as a foundational proof for the inseparability of love for the Prophet and love for his successor, Ali (as).

en.badr-shahin: My father (r) narrated to me from Sa’d bin Abdullah… from Muawiya bin Ammar from Ja’far bin Mohammed from his father from his grandfather

that the Prophet (s) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, some people will come on stages of light with their faces glittering like the full moon. They will be envied by the past and the last generations." The Prophet (s) kept silent for a while then added the statement three times. Omar bin al-Khattab asked: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you. Are they the shahids?" The Prophet (s) said: "They are shahids, but not the shahids that you know." Omar asked: "Are they the prophets?" The Prophet (s) said: "They are prophets, but not the prophets that you know." Omar asked: "Are they the successors of the prophets?" The Prophet (s) said: "They are successors of the prophets, but not the successors that you know." Omar asked: "Are they from the heavens or the earth?" The Prophet (s) said: "They are from the earth?" Omar said: "Tell me, who are they?" The Prophet (s) pointed to Ali (a) and said: "They are this one and his Shia. No one from Koreish hates him except the bastard, no one of Ansar hates him except the Jew, no one from the Arabs hates him except the whoreson, and no one from the human beings hates him except the scoundrel. O Omar, he who claims he loves me while he hates Ali is surely lying."
